fs-cold-4ways.back: Conduction (cold ground), convection (wind), radiation (open sky), evaporation (sweat, wet clothes).

fs-cold-trap.front: What is the hunter cold trap?
fs-cold-trap.back: Sweating on the climb, then sitting still to glass in damp clothes as the day cools.

fs-cold-sunset.front: About when is sunset in Kamloops on 31 October?
fs-cold-sunset.back: About 17:40, dark by about 18:14 (calculated). Clocks fall back 1 November.

fs-cold-habits.back: Start a little cold, vent before you sweat, swap a soaked base layer, puffy on and pad under when you stop.

fs-cold-moderate.back: Shivering slows or stops, drowsy but conscious. Core about 32 to 28 °C.

fs-cold-severe.back: No shivering, not conscious. Core under 28 °C. Check breathing and pulse up to 60 seconds.

fs-cold-umbles.back: Stumbles, mumbles, fumbles, grumbles: early hypothermia signs.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="The umbles, early signs of hypothermia: stumbles, tripping on flat ground; mumbles, slurred slow talk; fumbles, cannot work a zip; grumbles, cranky and careless. Any umble: stop, warm up, eat.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Watch for the umbles</text><rect x="20" y="50" width="170" height="84" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="105" y="84" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">Stumbles</text><text x="105" y="110" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">trips on flat ground</text><rect x="210" y="50" width="170" height="84" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="84" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">Mumbles</text><text x="295" y="110" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">slurred, slow talk</text><rect x="20" y="150" width="170" height="84" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="105" y="184" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">Fumbles</text><text x="105" y="210" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">cannot work a zip</text><rect x="210" y="150" width="170" height="84" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="295" y="184" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="middle">Grumbles</text><text x="295" y="210" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">cranky, careless</text><rect x="72" y="256" width="256" height="30" rx="6" fill="#2f3a2b"/><text x="200" y="277" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">Any umble: stop, warm, eat</text>

fs-cold-mild-care.back: Out of wind and wet, pad under, dry layers, head covered, heat to armpits, chest and back, warm sweet food if alert, rest 30 minutes.

fs-cold-mod-care.front: Care for moderate or severe hypothermia?
fs-cold-mod-care.back: Gentle, flat, no food or drink, insulate, big heat on the upper trunk, tarp outside, call 911 or SOS.
fs-cold-mod-care.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Moderate or severe step 3: large heat sources on the upper trunk. Small hand warmers are not enough for the core.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">3. Heat on the chest</text><rect x="0" y="240" width="400" height="60" rx="0" fill="#dfe6d3"/><rect x="80" y="226" width="240" height="14" rx="4" fill="#8a9a6b"/><rect x="80" y="196" width="240" height="30" rx="14" fill="#7c5a99"/><circle cx="70" cy="210" r="11.0" fill="#d9b48f"/><rect x="110" y="176" width="60" height="18" rx="5" fill="#e8590c"/><text x="200" y="120" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">Big heat on the chest</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Big heat on the upper trunk</text>
</svg>

fs-cold-handwarmers.front: Are small hand warmers enough to rewarm a cold core?
fs-cold-handwarmers.back: No. Use large heat sources on the trunk. Small packs only for hands and feet.

fs-cold-afterdrop.back: Cold blood from the limbs returning to the core when limbs are warmed or moved, dropping core temperature. Warm the trunk first, move gently.
fs-cold-afterdrop.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Afterdrop: rubbing or moving the arms and legs, or warming them first, sends cold blood from the limbs back to the core, which can drop core temperature further and upset the heart rhythm. Warm the trunk first and move the person gently.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Afterdrop: why gentle matters</text><rect x="120" y="60" width="160" height="170" rx="30" fill="#7c5a99"/><circle cx="200" cy="50" r="20.0" fill="#d9b48f"/><circle cx="200" cy="130" r="30.0" fill="#c0392b"/><text x="200" y="136" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff" text-anchor="middle">core</text><rect x="80" y="90" width="40" height="120" rx="15" fill="#9cc3e4"/><rect x="280" y="90" width="40" height="120" rx="15" fill="#9cc3e4"/><line x1="100" y1="150" x2="156" y2="142" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="168,140 155,135 157,149" fill="#4a7fb0"/><line x1="300" y1="150" x2="244" y2="142" stroke="#4a7fb0" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="232,140 243,149 245,135" fill="#4a7fb0"/><text x="60" y="250" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="start">Cold limb blood</text><text x="60" y="270" font-size="15" fill="#4a7fb0" text-anchor="start">rushes to the core</text><text x="200" y="290" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Warm the trunk first. Move them gently</text>
</svg>

fs-cold-nip-bite.front: Frostnip or frostbite: how to tell?
fs-cold-nip-bite.back: Frostnip is surface only and comes back fast with warming. Frostbite freezes tissue: white, waxy, hard.

fs-cold-fb-rub.front: Should you rub frostbite or rub snow on it?
fs-cold-fb-rub.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Frostbite step 2: do not rub it or rub snow on it. Blot dry. Rubbing damages frozen tissue.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">2. Do not rub it</text><ellipse cx="200" cy="150" rx="62" ry="36" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="173" y1="123" x2="227" y2="177" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="15" stroke-linecap="round"/><line x1="227" y1="123" x2="173" y2="177" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="15" stroke-linecap="round"/><text x="200" y="240" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#c0392b" text-anchor="middle">No rubbing, no snow</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">No rubbing. No snow on it</text>
</svg>

fs-cold-fb-refreeze.front: When should you NOT thaw frostbite?
fs-cold-fb-refreeze.back: When it could refreeze before you reach care. Thaw then refreeze does the most damage.

fs-cold-fb-water.front: Frostbite rewarming water temperature and time?
fs-cold-fb-water.back: 37 to 39 °C, about 30 minutes, until soft and red or purple.
fs-cold-fb-water.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Frostbite step 4: rewarm in water at 37 to 39 degrees Celsius, about 30 minutes, until soft and red or purple. Ibuprofen early. Do not walk on thawed feet.">
  <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
  <text x="200" y="26" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">4. Warm water bath</text><rect x="110" y="120" width="180" height="100" rx="10" fill="#4a7fb0"/><path d="M110 130 q 30 -10 60 0 t 60 0 t 60 0" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><ellipse cx="200" cy="150" rx="42" ry="24" fill="#d9b48f" stroke="#2f3a2b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="200" y="90" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#e8590c" text-anchor="middle">37 to 39 °C</text><text x="200" y="245" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">About 30 min, until soft</text><text x="200" y="288" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Warm, not hot. Test with a good hand</text>
</svg>
